topics.label: Introduction to the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: The subtopic outlines the lecture objectives, framework, and progression model for understanding the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Growth signaling pathways and mutational activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream intracellular cascades drive growth signal independence and sustained proliferation.

topics.label: Blocks to terminal differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells fail to exit the cell cycle and differentiate within hematopoietic lineages and intestinal crypt epithelium.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how alterations in p53 regulation and the balance of Bcl-2 family proteins prevent programmed cell death in cancer cells.

topics.label: Replicative immortality and cellular senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how telomere dynamics and p53-mediated stress responses trigger senescence, and how cancer cells bypass these limits through telomerase reactivation.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer cells rewire their bioenergetics via aerobic glycolysis, maintain tissue-specific metabolic profiles, and generate oncometabolites through Krebs cycle mutations.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how tumors overcome diffusion limits by altering the balance of pro- and anti-angiogenic signals to recruit new blood vessels.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and secondary colonization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the mechanisms of local invasion, lymphatic and vascular dissemination, metastatic inefficiency, and genomic traits that enable distant colonization.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The subtopic provides closing remarks, summarizes the integration of cancer hallmarks, and directs students to upcoming practical sessions.
